dimensions.assessment: Affects hydropower project licensees holding licenses issued before March 13, 2020, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
dimensions.evidence: a hydropower project with respect to which the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued a license before March 13, 2020

dimensions.assessment: Provides significant relief to eligible project developers by extending construction commencement deadlines by up to six years and enabling license reinstatements.
dimensions.evidence: extend... the period during which the licensee is required to commence construction of the covered project for not more than an additional 6 years

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending or revenue impacts are stated in the source text.
Provides targeted authority to FERC to modify construction commencement timelines and reinstate specific expired licenses outside standard Federal Power Act limits.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding section 13 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 806)... the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission may... extend... the period

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes extensions consisting of up to three consecutive two-year periods, lasting for a defined duration of up to six years.
dimensions.evidence: consist of not more than 3 consecutive 2-year periods

missing_information: The total number of hydropower projects or licensees eligible for extensions under this act is not listed.
importance_detail.rationale: S. 1020 authorizes FERC to extend construction deadlines by up to an additional six years for certain hydropower project licenses issued before March 13, 2020, and allows reinstatement of certain expired licenses.
